newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliamentary committee rejects tax code.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliamentary committee rejects tax code.

text.p: The budget committee of Russia's opposition-dominated lower house of parliament recommended on Monday that the State Duma reject the government's radical new tax code in favour of gradual adaptation of the tax system.
The committee's recommendations are not binding on the chamber, which is due to debate the tax code on Thursday.
But the decision was a setback for ministers who say the new package, which aims to help business by simplifying the tax system, is vital to put shaky state finances in order.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has pressed the Duma to pass the tax code by the end of the month, saying that otherwise the 1998 budget would be in jeopardy.

But the Duma committee, recommending a course of action directly contrary to the government's wishes, said in a statement it would be better for the government to propose a range of laws to address specific problems in the tax system rather than adopt a complete new tax code.
These, the committee said, would aid the 1998 budget.
The committee also complained that the code would reduce the tax burden on business at the expense of higher taxes on households.
The communist-dominated parliament and reform-minded government are engaged in a tug-of-war over economic management.
The Duma, which has little power to unseat the cabinet but can stall legislation, is holding up spending cuts prompted by a huge shortfall in tax revenue so far this year.
However, the deputies appeared reluctant to push the administration too far for fear President Boris Yeltsin might call new elections that could shift the political balance.

The International Monetary Fund, keen to promote a restructuring of the Russian economy, had made submission of the new tax code to the Duma by the government a condition for a resumption of lending to Russia this year.
